subject.title: Feature: trustedWebhooks for Discord — allow specific webhooks to trigger agent responses

question: Should Discord accept a new guild-scoped trusted webhook authority surface, and may that surface map webhook payloads onto a configured Discord user identity?
rationale: The requested behavior is narrower than `allowBots: true`, but it gives possession of a Discord webhook URL authority to enter agent sessions and the proposed `mapToUser` crosses authorization and session-identity boundaries.

options.title: Approve a narrow trusted-webhook contract
options.body: Allow maintainers to design an explicit webhook-id allowlist that can pass the bot-message gate, while keeping user impersonation/mapping either disallowed or separately constrained until its authorization semantics are defined.

options.title: Approve webhook-to-user mapping too
options.body: Permit `mapToUser` only with strict validation against configured guild users, clear audit/logging behavior, and tests proving it cannot bypass sender authorization or session isolation.

options.title: Decline Discord-specific webhook ingress
options.body: Keep Discord bot-message policy unchanged and direct external automation to the authenticated webhooks plugin or a ClawHub integration instead of adding another Discord config surface.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow trusted-webhook contract
recommendation.body: Allow maintainers to design an explicit webhook-id allowlist that can pass the bot-message gate, while keeping user impersonation/mapping either disallowed or separately constrained until its authorization semantics are defined.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Discord preflight ownership and adjacent review/merge history make this the best available routing candidate for the security/product decision.
